R/S (Rohit Selection) checks a company in 10 parts: quality of results (18), growth (12), cash flow (10), debt (10), shareholding (12), insider and bulk/block deals (8), valuation (12), 3-year price (8), stability (5) and risk (5). Valuation now works differently by sector (see \"R/S\'s valuation framework\" below); sectors without a method of their own, or with too little data, weigh half on a comparison with the sector\'s usual P/E and P/B and half on the company\'s own usual P/E of the last 3 years. Loss-making companies and those with a P/E under 3 (a one-off profit or old figures) get no valuation, and a quarter\'s earnings over 10 times the year\'s middle quarter count as one-off. Growth compares the sum of the last 4 quarters with the sum of the first 4; when the start is a loss or near zero, no percentage shows. For financial companies like banks, NBFCs and insurers the debt and cash-flow parts don\'t count, since borrowing to lend is their business. A part with no data gets a middling 50 in the score (neither good nor bad), so that a company good in just 2–3 parts and unknown in the rest doesn\'t rise above good companies with full data; the card says which parts had no data. The 0–100 score gives the grade: 75+ very strong, 62+ strong, 48+ fair, 35+ caution, below that avoid; when data is under 40%: \"Little data\". Stocks listed on NSE, NSE SME and BSE only are all included; SME companies report half-yearly, so their figures are in half-years. Data from Screener.in, NSE and Yahoo joins the cache once every evening — old quarters don\'t change, so only new results, shareholding and deals are added, and data older than 20 quarters / 5 years is dropped. The app fetches a new file up to twice a day and keeps just one copy. In the stock\'s detail, \"R/S history\" shows every quarter\'s results, the FII/DII/promoter stakes (▲ bought, ▼ sold), yearly cash flow and debt, and 3 years of price; its small file comes when you open that stock. Tap any part of the R/S card and its data opens beneath it: each quarter\'s results for quality and growth, a yearly table for cash flow and debt, promoter/FII/DII for shareholding, every deal for insiders (date, the day and time it reached NSE, name, who, buy/sell, shares, price, amount, mode, stake after the deal), P/E, fair value and the framework\'s full working for valuation, and a 3-year chart for price, stability and risk; the Insider and Bulk/Block lines open the same way, and a second tap closes them. Bulk/block deals have only just started being added, so their history builds up over time; insider trades and bulk/block deals are NSE\'s, so for BSE-only stocks that part stays empty. Not investment advice.
